clinician.trajectory_summary: A 13-year-old girl presented at 9 months of age with bilateral polycystic kidneys and a left flank palpable mass. Initial kidney function, blood pressure, and microalbuminuria were normal. At age 10, she developed cutaneous manifestations including facial erythema, angiofibromas, and hypopigmented maculas, which met the criteria for Tuberous Sclerosis. Concurrently, a repeat renal ultrasound at age 10 identified two nodules suggestive of angiomyolipomas in the left kidney. The known final diagnosis is TSC2/PKD1 Contiguous Gene Syndrome, which was confirmed by genetic testing, though the specific details of this genetic confirmation are not yet available.
